clip1.text: Fraud analysts usually review alerts one transaction at a time, from a long queue.
But the risky pattern often hides in the connections: several accounts paying one destination, money moving on within minutes, and shared devices.
Analysts rebuild that picture by hand, and an innocent link, like a family tablet, is easy to misread.
TraceGuard traces those connections automatically and writes an evidence-linked case brief with Gemini on Vertex AI.
The rule is simple: the graph decides, the AI explains, and every claim is checked before anyone sees it.
Here's case C-1. Four wallets send five transfers into A-07 within thirty minutes: seventeen thousand pesos in total.
Thirty minutes later, A-07 sends fifteen thousand five hundred onward. A payment made before the money arrived isn't counted.

clip2.text: Now I run the AI investigation. A fixed workflow runs every graph tool for this case, then Gemini explains the results.
Before anything is shown, every citation and every figure is checked against the tool output. This panel shows exactly what was verified, and which attempt passed.
Both rules flag a pattern that warrants review. The counterevidence comes from the tools: two senders aren't on the shared device, and less went out than came in.
Clicking a citation highlights the exact records on the graph, right beside the brief, so the analyst can check each claim in place.
I can also ask a follow-up question about the case. For example: who owns account A-22?
The case data can't answer that, so TraceGuard refuses to guess and says which records would be needed.

clip3.text: Case C-2 is three accounts sharing one tablet. Both rules were checked for each account, and none of them matched.
So the brief says the evidence is insufficient: a shared device on its own is not proof of anything.
In case C-3, A-19 forwards most of what it received to A-22, so the forwarding rule flags it for review.
But the trail reaches the edge of the data at A-22, so the next recipient and the intent are stated as unknown.
TraceGuard runs as one Cloud Run service, calling Gemini on Vertex AI through least-privilege access.
There are no API keys, the data is synthetic, and every model call is capped.
Connected evidence, cited, and honest about what it doesn't know. That's TraceGuard, built by team Chilli for the AI Builder Cup.
